newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SOCCER-GHANA EDGE IRISH IN YOUTH CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GHANA EDGE IRISH IN YOUTH CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Ghana, one of the favourites to take the world youth championship, overcame a surprisingly resilient Ireland with a hard-fought 2-1 victory on Tuesday.
Goals from Bashir Gambo and Mohamed Mochtar gave the 1995 world under-17 champions the three points in Alor Setar to go top of goup C.
Coach Francis Oki Akenteng said he was satisfied with the result.
"We played better and deserved to win," he said, adding: "I must confess the soggy pitch affected the way we played."
Oki said he was surprised at the quality of the Irish side, who dominated the first 15 minutes of the second half after being uninspiring in the opening period.
It was during this spell that Ireland equalised, Trevor Malloy tapping in Damien Duff's driven cross after Neil Fenn had set him free in the penalty area.
But Ghana, who led through Gambo's 28th minute goal, restored their advantage after 67 minutes when Mochtar scored after collecting a return pass from Joe Sam.

Irish coach Brian Kerr said: "We let in a soft goal, but came back strong to control the second half. We knew the Ghanians were stronger than us physically, so we decided to try to beat them technically."
Kerr prepared his team for Malaysia's tropical heat and humidity by having his players practise with plastic jackets over thick woollen clothing.
Ghana were joined on three points at the top of the group by the United States, who scored a last-minute goal against China through substitute Brian West to win 1-0 in Alor Setar.
In group B in Kuching, Brazil beat France 3-0 after South Korea and South Africa fought a goaless draw.
Uruguay joined Morocco at the top of group A with a 3-0 pummelling of Belgium in Shah Alam.
